Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

below preposition and adverb

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.51: ad mare īnfrā oppidum exspectābat
Cic. Fam. 9.26.1: suprā mē Atticus, īnfrā Verrius

īnfrā (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative; also an adverb

below (lower than)

Lower than a thing, not under it: īnfrā oppidum, below the town. As an adverb, below, or later in a text.

Other words

  • subter (+ accusative) — below, beneath

    preposition with the accusative (with the ablative in verse); also an adverb · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 3.20: quae suprā et subter

    Rare but classical (Lewis & Short). For “under”, see under.

Examples

  • in lectīcā cubāns ad mare īnfrā oppidum exspectābat

    he was waiting, lying in a litter, by the sea below the townCic. Verr. 2.4.51

  • in superiōre parte nāvigāre tantum, īnfrā etiam natāre concessum

    in the upper part one may only go by boat; below, swimming is allowed tooPlin. Ep. 8.8.6

  • per nūdam īnfrā glaciem fluentemque tābem liquēscentis nivis ingrediēbantur

    they were walking over the bare ice below and the running slush of melting snowLiv. 21.36.6

  • omnia haec, quae suprā et subter, ūnum esse

    that all these things, above and below, are oneCic. de Or. 3.20

See also under, above, down.
